title: How can a circle and its centre make an isosceles triangle?
description: Two places are marked on a circle and joined to its centre, and the two joining lines are shown to be equal. The same circle idea used for arcs in the example then gives the kind of triangle.
teaching_notes: One idea: every place on a circle is the same distance from its centre, so two lines from the centre to the circle are equal. Watch for children who pick the two places and then measure by eye instead of using the circle.

source: A circle is drawn with its centre marked, and some places are marked on the circle. Use them and the centre to form isosceles triangles.
video_script.why: The child has used arcs to find places that are the same distance from a centre and now uses a whole circle for the same idea.
video_script.substitution: The centre of the circle is one corner and two marked places on the circle are the other two corners.
video_script.anchor: A circle with its centre marked and some places marked on the circle
video_script.payoff_line: Any two places on the circle with the centre make an isosceles triangle.

final_answer.value: isosceles; equilateral when the two places are one radius apart
final_answer.spoken: any two places on the circle with the centre make an isosceles triangle, and two places one radius apart make an equilateral triangle

never_show: the words one radius apart before the answer beat
maths_rules: O is the centre; P and Q are on the circle
OP and OQ are radii of the same circle, so OP = OQ
two equal sides OP and OQ: triangle OPQ is isosceles
if PQ = OP then all three sides are equal and OPQ is equilateral
video_script.design: One idea: every place on a circle is the same distance from its centre. The circle stays in the anchor band; the working band holds the board solution.
